items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: INTERVIEWER: '...we were talking about Tony Almarico and how close you lived to him.' / INTERVIEWEE: 'No, no. I can remember as a kid hearing Tony practice... Tony did not know me from the neighborhood.'

ctx.x: I went to dances at high school proms and things on the roof of the Jung.

Yeah. Yeah, that's the reason I brought it up, because I know your father was associated with the Jung. I crashed a few dances up there. Yeah, you were young and you could get in. Back to that neighborhood, when we left off, I guess it was last time, we were talking about Tony Almarico and how close you lived to him. So when you were a kid did you go to his house?

No, no. I can remember as a kid hearing Tony practice, running scales from scale after scale after scale. That was before I even played trumpet. We'd be, you know, kids played around the neighborhood and everything, I can remember, hearing him play in the afternoon, whether he'd be warming up or just keeping his chops up or between jobs, I don't know. But Tony did not know me from the neighborhood. By the time I started playing in the Parisian Room we had moved out of the neighborhood just a matter of a year or…
